title: WSL: win-sshproxy exits with code 0 right after podman machine start in 6.1.4, so no API pipe
body:
### Issue Description

# WSL: win-sshproxy exits with code 0 right after `podman machine start` in 6.1.4, so no API pipe

## Issue description

On Windows with a WSL machine, `podman machine start` in 6.1.4 reports that API forwarding
is not available, because `win-sshproxy.exe` fails to start with exit code 0. No
`\\.\pipe\podman-machine-default` or `\\.\pipe\docker_engine` pipe exists after the start.
As a result, Podman Desktop and Docker API clients see no containers and no images.
The `podman` CLI still works because it connects over SSH.

This happens on every start: after a Windows reboot, and after a clean
`podman machine stop` / `podman machine start` with no leftover `gvproxy.exe` or
`win-sshproxy.exe` processes.

When I start `win-sshproxy.exe` by hand with the same arguments, it stays up and
the pipe works. So the binary itself works, and its environment is fine.

I did not see this before I updated to 6.1.4.

## Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Windows 11, Podman 6.1.4, rootless WSL machine (`podman machine init` with defaults).
2. Make sure that no `win-sshproxy.exe` or `gvproxy.exe` process is running.
3. `podman machine stop`
4. `podman --log-level=info machine start`
5. List the pipes: `Get-ChildItem \\.\pipe\ | Where-Object Name -match 'podman|docker'`

## Describe the results you received

```
Starting machine "podman-machine-default"
...
API forwarding for Docker API clients is not available due to the following startup failures.
	win-sshproxy.exe failed to start, exit code: 0 (see windows event logs)
Podman clients are still able to connect.
Machine "podman-machine-default" started successfully
```

- After the start, no `podman-machine-default` or `docker_engine` pipe exists.
- No `win-sshproxy.exe` process is running.
- `win-sshproxy.tid` in
  `%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\containers\podman\machine\wsl\podman-machine-default\`
  is written at the time of the start (`36384:13252`). So the proxy did start,
  wrote its thread ID, and then exited with code 0. Exit code 0 looks like a normal
  quit message, not a crash.
- The Windows Application, Defender, AppLocker and CodeIntegrity event logs have no
  entries for `win-sshproxy`. The Windows Event Log service is running. Defender shows
  no detections.

### Manual start works

The same binary, started by hand with a separate state directory, stays up and serves the pipe:

```
win-sshproxy.exe -debug podman-machine-default <separate-dir> \
  npipe:////./pipe/podman-machine-default \
  ssh://user@127.0.0.1:51367/run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock \
  C:\Users\<user>\.local\share\containers\podman\machine\machine
```

```
[debug] podman-machine-default: Setting up proxies
[info ] podman-machine-default: Listening on: \\.\pipe\podman-machine-default
[debug] podman-machine-default: Entering loop for quit
[debug] podman-machine-default: Unhandled message: 799
[debug] podman-machine-default: Socket forward established: //./pipe/podman-machine-default -> /run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock
```

My guess, not proven: something in the 6.1.x start path sends the quit message to the
proxy that it just started. One example is the orphan cleanup from #29765, if it
reads the new `win-sshproxy.tid`. The manual proxy uses a different state directory,
so the cleanup cannot find it, and it stays up.

### Possibly related: SSH port reassignment after reboot

After a Windows reboot, Podman Desktop shows
`detected port conflict on machine ssh port [62194], reassigning`.
Hyper-V/WinNAT reserves port blocks at boot. Port 62194 is in a reserved range:

```
netsh int ipv4 show excludedportrange protocol=tcp
     61497       61596
     ...
     62097       62196
     62197       62296
```

The machine moved to SSH port 51367, and the CLI works on that port. The proxy failure
also happens on later starts that have no port conflict, so I think the port conflict
is a separate trigger and not the cause.

## Describe the results you expected

`win-sshproxy.exe` stays running after `podman machine start`, and
`\\.\pipe\podman-machine-default` (and `docker_engine`) are available. Podman Desktop
then shows the containers and images.

## podman info output

```
Client: Podman Engine 6.1.4, API 6.1.4, go1.26.8, commit 464c15fec06f0074c916f9eff87c4806869c2833, windows/amd64
Server: Podman Engine 6.1.4, API 6.1.4, go1.26.9, commit 464c15fec06f0074c916f9eff87c4806869c2833, linux/amd64
Machine: wsl, rootless, 12 CPUs, 2 GiB, Fedora Linux 44 (Container Image), PID 1 is systemd
Windows: 10.0.26200.9448 (Windows 11 Enterprise)
WSL: 2.5.10.0, kernel 6.6.87.2-1
Install: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Podman (podman.exe, gvproxy.exe, win-sshproxy.exe dated 2026-10-12)
Podman Desktop is installed and starts at login. Its "Machine autostart" setting is at the default.
```

## Podman in a container

No

## Privileged or rootless

Rootless

## Upstream latest release

Yes (6.1.4)

## Additional environment details

Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (Sense) is active. No detections or blocks for the Podman binaries.

## Additional information

- I did not test whether Podman Desktop runs a start at the same time as the CLI start.
  The failure also happens when I run `podman machine stop` and then `podman machine start`
  from the CLI while Podman Desktop is open.
- Workaround: start `win-sshproxy.exe` by hand after `podman machine start`, as shown above.
